singleSourced.context:
You only said 'HLX' once." To which Morasky responds with what sounds like, "I did?"

Half-Life fans believe they've heard Morasky make this same flub before.

Supporting the rumors of HLX/Half-Life 3's existence is a report from longtime Valve reporter Tyler McVicker, who said in 2025 that the game isn't just in development, but "playable from end to end."

There's no indication that Valve plans to announce Half-Life 3 anytime soon, but fans of the first-person shooter franchise have gotten used to waiting.

"HLX has its own version, and so on and so forth."

Adding fuel to the fire, co-panelist David Feise, seated next to Morasky, immediately turned to him after the HLX comment and whispered "nice work," or possibly "nice one," obviously suggesting, hey man, you're not supposed to talk about that.

singleSourced.key: is its own one hour talk so come talk to us about that afterwards

singleSourced.context:
Feise then quickly puts an end to the answer as Morasky laughs nervously, saying Groups, which Morasky had been talking about leading up to the HLX remark, "is its own one-hour talk, so come talk to us about that afterwards."

There's no question that Morasky said HLX, and that Feise reacted.

singleSourced.key: good job you only said hlx once
singleSourced.value: Good job, you only said HLX once.
singleSourced.context:
In fact, at the end of the panel Feise leaned in and said, "Good job, you only said HLX once." Because this isn't the first time he's done it: Morasky appeared oh-so-close to saying "HLX" in 2025, although he was able to catch himself midway and shift gears, awkwardly, to "Alyx."
